item.title: Israeli settlers steal Palestinians' olives as attacks on harvest grow more violent
item.description:
By Pesha Magid and Lina Obeid

LUBBAN AL-GHARBI, West Bank, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Brought to tears as he recalled Israeli settlers hitting his cherished olive trees with sticks and taking off with the olives, Palestinian Ahmed Salem said he feared being attacked if he tried to intervene.

Settlers have intimidated Palestinians harvesting their olives in the occupied West Bank for decades, but this year, not only has violence increased sharply, theft has been widespread, according to Palestinians, Israeli rights groups and the UN.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Navy says seven vessels hit, warns US of wider response
item.description:
DUBAI, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

The IRGC added that three more vessels collided with mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases.

(Reporting by Tala Ramadan; Editing by Jacqueline Wong)

item.title: In Israel, Eisenkot tries quiet appeal to oust Netanyahu
item.description:
Gadi Eisenkot, the man who could unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, almost always dresses in plain black, speaks halting English and, reflecting the military culture that shapes him, responds in interviews in bullet-point lists.

For some voters, the 66-year-old Eisenkot's lack of charisma may be one of his greatest assets.

item.title: The key issues that will shape Israel's elections
item.description:
When Israel goes to the polls this month, voters will weigh in on military conscription, the economy and how the state should investigate its inability to prevent Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.

AFP looks at the key issues shaping the campaign as Israel gears up for elections on October 27.

- Accountability for October 7 -

item.title: Canada's Carney visits Turkey in push to ease US trade dependence
item.description:
By Maria Cheng and Tuvan Gumrukcu

ANKARA, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney will meet President Tayyip Erdogan in Turkey on Thursday, thefirst bilateral visit by a Canadian leader, as he seeks to expand trade ties and reduce reliance on the United States.

Carney and Erdogan are expected ‌to sign a declaration deepening cooperation in four areas including defence and energy, a person briefed on the matter said. A Turkish diplomatic source said the bilateral ties will be upgraded to a "strategic partnership."

item.title: China, Djibouti say all countries should enjoy freedom of navigation in Red Sea
item.description:
BEIJING, Oct 22 (Reuters) - All countries should enjoy freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, China and Djibouti said in a joint statement following a meeting of their foreign ministers in Beijing, expressing concern about the deteriorating security situation.

Djibouti sits on the other side of theBab ed-Mandeb Straitfrom Yemen, where Iran-backedHouthis have been battling Saudi-backed governmentforces and seeking to control the whole Yemeni Red Sea coast, disrupting some shipping.

item.title: Washington orders US embassy staff, families to leave Saudi Arabia
item.description:
The United States has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a social media post explaining the measure.

item.title: Exclusive-Senior UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh enters race for UN chief
item.description:
By Maha El Dahan

DUBAI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Senior UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh entered the race to become the next United Nations secretary-general on Wednesday, injecting a prominent Middle Eastern candidate into a contest that has struggled to produce a consensus choice among the Security Council’s most powerful members.

Nusseibeh, a former UAE ambassador to the UN for more than a decade, told Reuters she would seek to restore the world body’s role as a diplomatic problem-solver at a time of mounting global crises.

item.title: UAE nominates official to lead UN
item.description:
The UAE nominated Wednesday its foreign ministry official Lana Nusseibeh to run in the contest to lead the UN as none of the six existing candidates has emerged as a clear front-runner.

Lana Nusseibeh is a well-regarded minister of state at the United Arab Emirates foreign ministry, having previously represented Abu Dhabi at the UN.

item.title: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
item.description:
By Rami Ayyub, Humeyra Pamuk and Timour Azhari

JERUSALEM/ISTANBUL/DUBAI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.

The order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam and two people were killed in a drone attack on an oil field.

item.title: Tunisia military court sentences opposition figure Olfa Hamdi to four years in prison
item.description:
By Tarek Amara

TUNIS, Oct 21 (Reuters) - A Tunisian military court sentenced opposition politician Olfa Hamdito four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the military to disobey orders, her lawyer said on Wednesday, the latest move against opponents of President Kais Saied.

Hamdi, the leader of the Third Republic Party who holds US citizenship, wasdetained at Tunisia's main airport after disembarking from a flight in February.

She had been living abroad and previously served as CEO of Tunisia's national carrier Tunisair.

item.title: US sanctions Greece-, Panama-based law firm over aid to Iranian shipping
item.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 21 (Reuters) - The US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Wednesday on Karnakis & Karnakis, a law firm based in Greece and Panama, saying it had for years provided legal assistance to Iranian shipping networks.

The US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network also issued an administrative subpoena to advance an investigation into a Greek bank over potential ties to Iran, according to a Treasury statement, which did not name the bank.

item.title: Turkey egg donor scam allegedly sold clients on promise of blond babies
item.description: An investigation triggered by a husband’s tip has led to at least 45 arrests in an alleged network that sold Turkish donor eggs to foreign clients seeking Scandinavian ancestry.

item.title: After Syria war, Druze in Golan Heights warm to Israel
item.description:
For many Druze in the Golan Heights, participating in an Israeli election used to be done in secret, but when Israel holds national polls next week, Fadi Damaqsi will be casting his ballot proudly.

"It's crucial for all Israeli citizens to vote," said Damaqsi, from the Golan Heights town of Ein Qiniye. "It's a right, but it's also an honour."

item.title: US sanctions law firm based in Panama, Greece over Iran shipping ties
item.description: The Treasury Department accused Karnakis and Karnakis of registering shipping companies linked to Iran's so-called shadow fleet.
